resources.name: regional-rounding-npu-v1
command:
import os,sys,subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from scripts.job import atomic
out=Path("{run}");rows=[]
for kind in ("settle","timed"):
 command=[sys.executable,"-m","scripts.diagnose_region_batch","--config","configs/hb-multiscale-x-"+kind+".json","--device","npu:0","--precision","bf16","--threads","1","--output-dir",str(out/kind)]
 with (out/(kind+".log")).open("w") as log:
  result=subprocess.run(command,stdout=log,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=600)
 rows.append(dict(kind=kind,command=command,exit_code=result.returncode));atomic(out/"children.json",dict(source=os.environ["TIDE_SOURCE_COMMIT"],children=rows))
sys.exit(any(r["exit_code"] for r in rows))

cpu_replay.scope: CPU serial replay of each recorded NPU three-update parameter set; same CPU reference kernels

native_restore.cpu_replay_recipe: Use native/regional/reference.py read_bundle(fixture). For each native-bfloat16-train-w1/w4 tensor bundle, replace all nine parameter tensors with parameter.NAME from that bundle; run_reference(data,device=cpu,dtype=bfloat16,mode=train,repeats=1) serially with one ATen/OMP thread. Compare grad.parameter.v_weight[9,18] and all named tensors. This tests gradient sensitivity, not a restored optimizer trajectory.
native_restore.conclusion: Observed initial FP32 second-layer parameter differences and later BF16-scale gradient discrepancy; CPU serial replay does not reproduce the selected v_weight discrepancy. Contribution accumulation order, backend backward arithmetic and their propagation remain unresolved; no universal cause is claimed.
